SUMMARY.md:
> The antipode of any latitude/longitude and what digging straight through the Earth to it would mean, from the `api.tasta.space` hub: where you come out (land, sea or Antarctic ice, from Natural Earth 1:10m shapes), the nearest shore, tunnel length, fall time through a uniform and a real Earth, top speed, the Kola borehole for comparison, and a verdict. GET only, JSON in a {"data": ..., "meta": ...} envelope, no key needed (anonymous callers get 30 requests a minute and 1,000 a day per IP, shared across every API on the hub).
>
> Sources: the documentation page https://api.tasta.space/dig and the hub rules at https://api.tasta.space/docs, with /dig probed live on 2026-10-23 (Bucharest, Madrid, Sydney, Honolulu, both poles, and a 422 for lat=91).
>
> Not modelled: format=text (one plain-text line) and /dig/image, which returns an SVG or PNG cross-section rather than JSON. Unverified: a null `nearest_land`.country (every nearest coast probed had one).
A dig straight through the centre of the Earth from one point to its antipode.
